title: Orphaned baby marmoset named after UK detective who saved him | CNN
text:
Source: CNN

Detective Constable Gino Ferrara normally spends his days investigating rape and serious sexual offences on London’s streets. But on November 11, the detective encountered a tiny, scared, baby monkey trapped in a south London shed.

“When I saw the marmoset I was shocked. The yard where he was being kept smelt awful, like feces, and there were dogs running loose and barking constantly,” Det. Con. Ferrara said in apress releasefrom the UK Metropolitan Police.

“You could hear this little monkey screaming. We could just tell he was scared; he looked shocked and confused,” Det. Con. Ferrara added.

Officers were at the property following a warrant by the Met’s Trident unit in October connected with a separate investigation into the alleged possession of a firearm. They discovered the 5-month-old marmoset locked in a bird cage in a shed and passed the intelligence onto wildlife specialists.

That’s when Det. Con. Ferrara, who volunteers his time with wildlife crime officers, quickly arranged to get help from a local sanctuary calledMonkey World. He and Dr. Alison Cronin from the rescue went out to the property and couldn’t believe what they saw.

Dr. Cronin says she was surprised the baby marmoset was still alive because “he is so young and was left on his own in a cold garden shed in a bird cage.”

“It must have been lonely, scary, and very cold, especially for a youngster who should still be carried by his parents,” Dr. Cronin added, according to the press release.

The property’s occupants willingly surrendered the monkey to officers claiming they were just taking care of him for a friend, according to police.

He was then taken to Monkey World and introduced to an adult black-tufted marmoset named Minty. He instantly tried to climb onto her back as if she were his mother.

Now that baby monkey has a name — Gino — after the detective who changed his life.

“We are so pleased for Gino that he has found a mum in Minty and that he is now getting the specialist care that he needs,” Dr. Cronin said.

“To see that I’ve played a part in ensuring Gino has gone to a good home makes me feel very proud,” Det. Con. Ferrara said.

So far no arrests have been made but an animal welfare investigation is underway.
